children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

informal_arrangement.description: Whether the claimant is looking after someone else's child through an informal arrangement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello, yes I'm inquiring about my child. I have one child, Alex, who is 11 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 11 years old.

Now I need to understand your living situation. **Do you live with Alex in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great. Since Alex is 11 years old and lives with you in the UK, you meet the basic criteria.

Now I need to ask: **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (Remember, only one person can get Child Benefit for a child.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Just a couple more questions to make sure I have all the information:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care?** In other words, do you provide for Alex's day-to-day needs such as food, clothes, and general upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, I look after Alex day-to-day - I provide food, clothes, and take care of all their needs. But I should mention that I'm not Alex's parent or their official carer. It's more of an informal arrangement where I look after them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is an important detail. You mentioned it's an informal arrangement where you look after Alex.

**Can you tell me more about this situation? Specifically:**
1. **Is your local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance costs?**
2. **Are Alex's parents still involved, or what are the circumstances that led to you looking after Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
No, the local council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance - I cover all those costs myself. 

As for the circumstances, Alex's parents aren't able to look after them at the moment, so I've stepped in to care for Alex. It's just an informal family arrangement we've worked out between us.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. That's very helpful.

Just to confirm I have everything I need: **Have Alex's parents (or anyone else who might be responsible for Alex) agreed that you should be the one to claim Child Benefit?** This is important because only one person can claim for the same child, and if there's any disagreement, HMRC would need to decide.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's all sorted. There's no disagreement - everyone's agreed that I should be the one to claim Child Benefit for Alex since I'm the one looking after them full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:

✓ Alex is 11 years old (under 16)  
✓ You live with Alex in the UK  
✓ You're responsible for Alex's care and provide for all their needs  
✓ The local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance  
✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex  
✓ Everyone has agreed you should be the one to claim  

The rules allow for Child Benefit when you have an informal arrangement to look after a relative's child, as long as the local council isn't contributing to their costs - which applies to your situation.

**Next steps:** You can now make a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. 

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, so you may want to consider that when deciding whether to claim.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
